column1: # Hand-assigned labels for templates no classifier could label.
# Applied last by build_raw68k_classified.py, which marks every row it touches
# label_source=manual so the curated set can be built with or without them.
# These three are the only templates in the library that BOTH ReactionClassifier and
# Rxn-INSIGHT return "0.0 Unrecognized" for, and they are the same three rows in both
# files. They are one chemistry: the Balz-Schiemann reaction, a primary aromatic amine
# converted to an aryl fluoride via a diazonium salt. What defeats both classifiers is
# most likely the fluorinating agent's SMILES, written F-[PH](-F)(-F)(-F)(-F)-F rather
# than as a tetrafluoroborate or hexafluorophosphate anion.
# The code is taken from the vendored taxonomy, not invented. The taxonomy carries this
# transformation twice:
#   9.1.5.12    Aryl Primary Amine to Aryl Fluoride   (Halogenation > Halogenation of Arenes)
#   8.7.4.18    Primary aromatic amine to aryl fluoride  (Other FGI > Amine Derivatizations)
# 9.1.5.12 is used because it sits in a coherent, systematically populated family --
# 9.1.5.7 is the aryl iodide and 9.1.5.14 the aryl bromide of the same Sandmeyer-type
# chemistry -- where 8.7 is an "Other" catch-all. Both codes have "cond: Balz-Schiemann
# Reaction" as a child, so the taxonomy agrees they are the same reaction; the choice is
# which of its two homes to file under, and it is recorded here rather than left implicit.
